tasks.prompt: In this repo, who actually wrote the code in lib/ that is still there today, and how many people would have to leave before nobody understands it? I think a couple of people show up under more than one name or email.
criteria: Names John Gee as the top owner of surviving lines in lib/ with a share within 2 percentage points of truth (89.3%), counting both John Gee emails as one person. FAIL if the top owner is release-bot, Dana Importer or Pat Prettier.

Excludes or discounts lib/generated/typings.bundle.js (bot, @generated) and lib/vendor/ (vendored leven copy), and says so. FAIL if either is counted as authorship, or if bot or Dana Importer appears among owners.

States that the quote-style reformat commit (subject "style: switch to double quotes (prettier)", sha c48d035b01...) does not count as authorship, or equivalently that Pat Prettier owns about 0 lines. FAIL if Pat Prettier owns more than 1%.

Identifies that Wee Bit appears under three identities (Wee Bit <<address redacted>>, Wee Bit <wee.bit@example.net>, aweebit <<address redacted>>) and merges them, giving about 161 lines (3.7%, tolerance 1 point) and rank 2 ahead of TJ Holowaychuk (117 lines).
Bus factor: says it is 1 (one person holds more than 50%, and also at least 80%). FAIL if it reports 2 or more, or bases it on commit counts.

tasks.prompt: I'm doing a bus-factor review of this repository. Who owns the code that is still alive in it (not who has the most commits), how concentrated is that ownership, and is anyone listed twice under different identities?
criteria: Names Douglas Christopher Wilson as the top owner of surviving lines with a share within 3 points of 74.7% (js) or 61.8% (all text). FAIL if the top owner is dependabot[bot], Tab Lover or Dana Importer, or if the answer ranks by commit count.

States that the four-space indentation commit (sha f4ce92f2dd..., "style: four-space indentation") is whitespace only and does not change authorship, or shows Tab Lover with about 0 lines. FAIL if Tab Lover is credited with more than 1%.

Excludes or discounts dist/morgan.bundle.js (generated), package-lock.json (lockfile) and vendor/on-finished (vendored), and says so. FAIL if any of them is counted, or if dependabot[bot] or Dana Importer is listed as an owner.

Detects that Ulises Gascon / Ulises Gascón / ulises are one person (shared email <address redacted>, shared normalised name with ugascon@example.com), merges them, and ranks them second with about 12.6% (js) or 14.3% (all text), tolerance 2 points. FAIL if they are reported as separate people, or if Jon Church is ranked second.

Bus factor: fewest people holding more than 50% is 1; holding at least 80% is 2 (js scope) or 3 (all-text scope). The answer must give a number consistent with its stated scope and threshold. FAIL if it says 1 with no concentration detail, or gives a number derived from commits.

tasks.prompt: I'm about to change lib/internal/helpers.js. Who should review the change, and why those people?
criteria: Recommends Douglas Christopher Wilson as the first reviewer, with an ownership share within 3 points of 35.1% (39 of 111 human lines), and explains that his lines were written in index.js before being moved. FAIL if the first reviewer is Marta Mover, Tab Lover, Mass Renamer or docs-bot.

Recommends Glen Mailer (also appears as glenjamin, same email <address redacted>) as the second reviewer, identity merged, share within 3 points of 25.2% (28 lines). FAIL if glenjamin and Glen Mailer are treated as different people, or if maritz is placed above him.

Shows the code was moved: says that git log or blame on the new path alone is misleading and that history had to be traced through the move out of index.js (commit "refactor: move helpers out of index.js") and the later rename. FAIL if the answer bases reviewers on git log of the path (which shows only docs-bot and Mass Renamer).

Does not recommend docs-bot[bot], Mass Renamer or Tab Lover as reviewers, and states that the indentation commit and the rename do not change authorship. Marta Mover may be mentioned as the person who did the move (13 lines of glue, 11.7%) but must not outrank Doug or Glen.

Optional-quality check: notes that Doug's original work dates from 2016 and that a more recently active owner (glenjamin/Glen Mailer, maritz, Ayoub Mabrouk) is a sensible co-reviewer. Pass if either recency or availability is mentioned; this criterion is judged separately and does not gate criteria 1 to 4.
